findings.fix: lower reporting-api container requests to about 10m CPU / 8Mi memory (well above p95 usage); re-check after a longer sampling window before cutting further

diagnosis.summary: Checked analytics: 3 workloads, no problem pods. ingest-worker pinned at its 50m CPU limit (at-limit share 1.0) — throttled, not idle, left alone. cache's requests already tiny (~$0.25/mo), not worth changing. reporting-api is the real over-provisioner: 300m/256Mi requested vs ~0/3Mi p95 usage, ~$7.69/mo idle; suggest 10m/8Mi. Caveat: only 10 samples in ~2 min, so confidence medium; verify with a longer window first.

findings.fix: Point the checkout-web trust volume at the internal-ca ConfigMap (ca.crt of Internal Services CA 2026) instead of legacy-ca, and restart the pods so nginx verifies payments-api with the correct CA.
findings.name: checkout-web
findings.root_cause: Checkout 502s: checkout-web's nginx cannot verify the payments-api upstream TLS cert ('unable to verify the first certificate') because it still mounts the legacy-ca bundle, while post-migration payments-api is signed by Internal Services CA 2026.

diagnosis.summary: payments-api is up and ready; the 502s come from checkout-web. Its nginx proxies /pay to https://payments-api:443 and fails the upstream TLS handshake with 'unable to verify the first certificate'. checkout-web mounts its trust store from the legacy-ca ConfigMap (Legacy Services CA 2021), while the migrated payments-api presents a certificate issued by Internal Services CA 2026 (internal-ca ConfigMap, valid, not expired). Fix: switch checkout-web's trust volume to internal-ca.
